title: Estate-wide RBAC grants
description: Role assignments that exceed a single repo's resource-group scope, applied idempotently by scripts/apply-role-grants.ps1 during onboarding. Two cases: 'subscription' scope (e.g. read access for a user-assigned identity), and 'resource' scope on a resource OUTSIDE the identity's own repo RG (e.g. the claude-runner-test broker needing rights on an Azure Arc machine in rg-homelab) — which the repo's own SP cannot assign because it is Owner of only its RG. Repo-scoped RBAC on a resource INSIDE the repo's RG still belongs in that repo's own Bicep instead.

comment.description: Why this grant exists — required reading for whoever reviews changes here.

identityName.description: Name of the user-assigned managed identity receiving the roles.

scope.description: Assignment scope. 'subscription' = the whole subscription. 'resource' = a single resource named by scopeResourceId (for cross-RG grants the owning repo's SP cannot make itself). Anything inside the identity's own repo RG belongs in that repo's Bicep.

scopeResourceId.description: Full ARM resource ID to scope the assignment to. Required when scope is 'resource'; ignored for 'subscription'.

roles.description: Built-in role names to assign (e.g. Reader, Log Analytics Reader). All roles in one grant share the same condition (or lack of one) — a role that can't carry an ABAC condition (e.g. Container Registry Repository Catalog Lister) needs its own separate grant entry for the same identity, same as the existing pattern of multiple entries per identity.

condition.description: Optional Azure ABAC condition expression, applied to every role in this grant. Only meaningful for ABAC-enabled roles (e.g. the ACR 'Container Registry Repository Reader/Writer/Contributor' roles on a registry with roleAssignmentMode 'rbac-abac') — assigning an ABAC-enabled role WITHOUT a condition grants registry-wide access, not repository-scoped access. Requires conditionVersion. NOTE idempotency caveat: apply-role-grants.ps1's existing-assignment check matches on (assignee, role, scope) only — it does not compare condition text, so editing a condition on an already-applied grant will not re-apply it. Delete the stale assignment (az role assignment delete) to force recreation.

conditionVersion.description: Azure ABAC condition syntax version. Required when condition is set; "2.0" is the only currently supported value.
